subject: The AI bill you forgot to cancel
subject_line: The AI bill you forgot to cancel
preview: You might be paying $130 a month so three different tools can fix the same bug. This week: which coding subscription to keep, and which to cancel before renewal.
lede: You might be paying $130 a month so three different tools can fix the same bug. Copilot Pro is $10. Cursor Pro is $20. Claude Max starts at $100. Grok SuperGrok is another $30 if it is sitting open in a second tab.
verification: Prices verified from official pages, rechecked 2026-08-25. ChatGPT US-dollar amounts were not reliably exposed on the official pricing page, so they are not listed here. Verify before buying.
public_editorial_html:
Morning.

I keep seeing the same pattern in people's tool invoices: Copilot Pro, Cursor Pro, and Claude Max all running at once, each doing a version of the same job. That's $130 a month — and the math isn't the problem. The problem is that most of it is overlap. You're not getting three times the output. You're getting three billing cycles and a context-switching tax.

This week I checked the official pricing pages for the main coding AI subscriptions (verified 2026-08-25) and the conclusion is pretty simple: pick a lane. The good news is the lanes are actually distinct, and one of them is probably enough.

The bill

Copilot Pro is $10/month. Cursor Pro is $20/month (Hobby free, Pro+ $60, Ultra $200, Teams $40/seat). Claude Max starts at $100/month — Claude Pro is $20/month or $200/year, but Max is what you need for terminal-agent work. Add them up and you're at $130 for the same coding job. Grok SuperGrok is another $30, Plus is $100.

Keep

Copilot Pro ($10) if you want inline completions in the editor you already use. Cursor Pro ($20) if you want an AI-native editor with multi-file context. Claude Max ($100+) only if your workflow genuinely involves long terminal agent sessions on a real repo. Not for chat. Not for occasional questions.

Cut

The overlapping surface. If you have Cursor, you probably don't need Copilot. If you have Copilot and it's working, Cursor is a bigger commitment than an upgrade. Protocol: 45 minutes, one real bugfix, score edit burden, keep the winner, cancel the rest 48 hours before renewal.

Before you renew

Grok SuperGrok ($30) / Plus ($100) — verify current tier names on X before committing. ChatGPT GPT-5.4 recorded 2026-08-26: no reliable US-dollar Plus/Pro price was exposed on the official page — don't guess a number, verify openai.com/pricing before you lock in an annual. Claude: chat plan and Claude Code are not the same invoice.

Worth a look

HtmlSlides — $9.90/month at launch. Test against your actual presentation workflow before adding a seat. Skip for now unless slides are a real recurring pain point. Whop CLI — free to install, transaction fees only if selling. Keep if you're already on Whop, skip otherwise.

What are you paying for that you stopped using?

See you next week.

— AIToolsEssentials

new_listings.name: HtmlSlides
new_listings.note: Pro is $9.90/month at launch. Interactive HTML decks. Test against Gamma on one real presentation before you add a seat. Novelty is not a job.

new_listings.name: Whop CLI
new_listings.note: $0 to install. Terminal control for Whop products and checkout. Relevant if you sell on Whop. Not a second subscription if you do not sell there.

watch_list.note: Chat plan and Claude Code are not the same job. Do not assume one invoice covers both personalities.

keep_one.title: Claude Code vs Cursor vs Copilot
keep_one.rule: Keep one paid coding surface. Copilot for inline completions in the editor you already have. Cursor if you want an AI-native IDE. Claude Code if the job is a terminal agent on a repo. Paying for two is overlap. Paying for three is $130 a month for the same bug.

protocol: Forty-five minutes. One real bugfix. Run it in each seat you actually pay for. Score first-output acceptance and edit burden. Keep the winner. Cancel the rest 48 hours before renewal.
keep_cut_rule: One weekly job. One paid tool. If two invoices own the same Friday, one of them is leaving.
